svg.text: SLAP2 F0 network: inputs, box blind spot, outputs (v9 fine-tuned, the default)

One forward pass predicts the baseline F0 and the noise variance σ² at every pixel and frame. The output at (t, r, c) never sees the movie within ±8 frames and ±4 px of itself, so events there cannot leak into it.
2 Branches: each sees a different part of the window
4 What the output at (t, r, c) sees
loss on the central 192 frames × 48 × 48 px (dashed)
prediction tiles whole trials the same way
log (variance map ÷ g · M): events add variance
Channels 3–5 are whole-trial maps, constant in
time: each frame enters with weight 1/T,
a negligible leak through the blind spot.
per-frame 3×3 conv, dilation 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 4 (blocks 3–7 at ½ res)
and a causal temporal conv, kernel 3, dilation 1, 2, 4, …, 64
then shifted by 9 frames: sees frames t−263 … t−9, ±23 px
Future branch: the same on reversed time (t+9 … t+263)
1×1×1 conv 5 → 24, then 5 blocks: a 2×3 conv that sees rows r−d … r
only (dilation 1, 1, 1, 2, 4; blocks 3–5 at ½ res) and a symmetric
temporal conv, dilation 1, 2, 4, 8, 16; then shifted down 5 rows.
Rotated 0, 90, 180, 270°, the four see every pixel outside the box,
up to 22 px away, in frames t−31 … t+31: the output frame too
fractional deviation Σ(movie − M) / Σ M over squares of half-width
8, 16, 32 px and the whole window, each minus the box, in frame t
and over frames t−3 … t+4: shared brightness changes, even fast ones
The pixel's own long window, and its whole-trial maps
mean W̄ and variance of the movie at (r, c) over 9 ≤ |dt| ≤ 262:
log (W̄ / M), log (variance / g W̄), share of the window with data;
and log M, log variance ratio, log variance factor at (r, c).
Enter at the output only: inside a branch they would reach hidden frames
per pool square, the surround fitted as a M − d · ∇M + b · ∇²M;
the change that d and b make at the pixel, and its own ∇M / M, ∇²M / M
between the mean image and the window mean
Outputs at every pixel and frame
σ² (t, r, c): noise variance, counts²
Heads start at 0: the untrained network predicts F0 = M.
a Time × row through the output's column: the whole window
b Zoom on the output: frames t−40 … t+40, rows ±26
c Rows × columns in frame t (no past or future branch here)
the box, up to 22 px away
Mean loss: Σ w (y − F0)² / photon variance at M. It is minimized by the conditional mean, so the baseline is unbiased at any brightness (a robust likelihood on skewed low counts is not).
Noise loss: 0.1 × Gaussian negative log-likelihood of movie − activity around F0 (held fixed), so σ² learns the actual spread around the baseline.

Targets: simulated windows (real trials as templates, with fast brightness changes, realistic low counts; v10 adds motion, focus and local warps) → the true baseline; real windows → movie − GIAnT's activity.
v9: pretrained 3000 steps on simulations from v6r, then fine-tuned 1700 steps on half real, half simulated windows; up/down flips only; half of the windows end or start at a trial edge.
